question: Shortcomings in the implementation of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1362 are putting Finnish and other Nordic trailer manufacturers at a disadvantage compared with other operators and could increase real CO₂ emissions.

The current calculation model treats structurally heavier trailers unfairly, especially side‑loading trailers, because they are classed in the same vehicle category as lighter box trailers. This results in disproportionate emission‑reduction requirements and penalises fleets that actually reduce empty runs and total emissions in practice.

Equipment like this is used in the defence industry and in the transport of explosives. This raises the question as to whether any thought was given to the impact that these measures would have on critical transport operations. In practice, the emissions limits that will enter into force in 2028 cannot be achieved for this type of fleet.

Consequently, the manufacture and marketing of this equipment could well come to an end. At the same time, manufacturers are being subjected to substantial fines in cases where it is not technically possible to satisfy the requirements. Will the Commission: 1.
review the VECTO classification so that side‑loading trailers are given their own sub‑category;
introduce correction factors that take account of logistical efficiency; and
reassess the use of fines in cases where it is not realistic for the requirements to be satisfied?
answer: EN On behalf of the European Commission (3.6.2026) Regulation (EU) 2022/13621 sets rules to determine the performance of heavy-duty trailers with regard to their influence on the CO2 emissions, fuel consumption, energy consumption and zero-emission driving range of motor vehicles.
The performance determination is done using a physics-based calculation model that considers the main trailer characteristics, such as mass, to reflect the real-world performance of the trailer.

In that context, a trailer that is made heavier by features such as a side-loading doors will result in higher CO2 emissions of the towing vehicle during real-world operation compared to an identical trailer with a lower mass.

The CO2 emission reduction targets for trailers and semi-trailers set in Regulation (EU) 2019/12422 will only start applying as of the reporting period of the year 2030, meaning that emission premiums do not apply until that date.

The targeted amendment to the Regulation3 proposed by the Commission in December 2025 provides trailer manufacturers with an additional flexibility easing compliance with the 2030 targets by allowing them to collect more emission credits in the years before 2030.

In parallel, the Commission is preparing a Delegated Act amending the Regulation to include additional reporting parameters that allow for identifying specific types of trailers, and is notably analysing the specific situation of trailers designed for the transport of explosives and ammunition. A review of the Regulation is foreseen in 2027.
At this stage, the Commission cannot prejudge the outcome of the review on specific questions, including the excess CO2 emissions premium level, as it will depend on the underlying analysis.
